scope: Posthoc read-only diagnosis of saved initial binary relation matrices for learned logical-NEQ pairs. This is not another experiment, producer run, propagation run, oracle query or certificate replay.

matrix_semantics.phase: phase index 0 in each archived policy, after its initial propagation under the scenario initial anchors
matrix_semantics.matrix_field: run.phases[0].outcome.relations; this is the completed initial closure, not initial_relations before propagation
matrix_semantics.pair_coordinate: same original side_order indices in both policies; ordered color pair (a,b) uses bit 4*(a-1)+(b-1)
matrix_semantics.baseline_already_excludes_equal: baseline relation mask AND 0x8421 is zero
matrix_semantics.new_initial_binary_tightening: baseline relation mask AND 0x8421 is nonzero and logical-NEQ initial closure relation mask AND 0x8421 is zero
matrix_semantics.domain_comparison: Unary domains are saved for both endpoints as context; binary tightening need not shrink either unary domain.

limitations: The 311 denominator counts repeated pair references across modes, not 311 distinct physical edges, distinct graphs, independent discoveries or new theorems.

Already excluded means implied by the saved baseline closure under that scenario initial anchors. This does not assert that every certificate is globally redundant under all possible anchors or states.
A same-color pair retained by the baseline matrix is only locally allowed by that binary closure. It is not a complete raw-graph extension witness.
Only phase 0 and the pairs actually learned by the logical-NEQ policy are examined. This is not a census of all states, all pairs, all possible relations or all planar graphs.
The added raw-graph certificate can be unconditional even when its phase-0 effect is redundant. Neither count alone establishes runtime improvement or a larger completion set.
Source hashes and stored matrix values were checked here. The separate formal saved-artifact checker establishes certificate/trace validity; it was not repeated by this diagnostic.
No graph-isomorphism quotient is used; unique keys refer to the frozen literal drawing identity, and key-pair uniqueness uses original side identifiers.
